name: H-A Axial orientation + tip/junction heads with geometry-aware decoding (this session's lane)
layers: All 19 GeoDAWN bands via structure tensor + edge ranks (rtp, tmi, tmi_hg/vg, tc, grav hg/vg/slope, det_elev, cond_surf, depth_to_base_surf, geod strain trio, seismicity proximity)
signature: Orientation-coherent linear edge chains (cos 2θ, sin 2θ axial field) with Gaussian tip/junction heat (σ = 1.5 px); decoded by orientation-gated hysteresis + orientation-aware NMS; traces extended past mapped tips along predicted strike while probability support persists
why_off_catalogue: Mapped tips are systematically short: tip zones fall below mapping resolution (~500 m per fault in one published seismic array; 100–200 m DEM truncation in a rift study). Continuations and splays past tips are exactly the segments missing from USGS/INGENIOUS; the tip head + orientation march is a detector for them, not a re-plotter of mapped traces
differs: No family repository (GEMSDOE…66GEMSDOE) used multi-branch orientation/tip heads or orientation-aware NMS/hysteresis. Closest relatives: h33d-analog-tip-stepover (geologic analog placement, no learned orientation), GEMSDOE53 tiprelay (relay physics, no heads), 66GEMSDOE LIDAR-01 (ranked but NOT implemented — native-resolution scarps, different layers)
rank_note: Rank 1: expected +0.01–0.03 HOLDOUT-DTI over isotropic decoding at matched mass; medium cost. Gateable on tip-adjacent recovery — implemented and validated this session

name: H-B Geodetic strain-localization corridor detector
layers: geod_2ndinv (strain-rate second invariant), geod_shearrate, geod_dilaterate (+ their gradients)
signature: Ridge/edge lines in the geodetic strain-rate field: interseismic deformation localizes on locked/creeping fault patches at mm/yr scale, producing coherent linear gradients even where no scarp or magnetic contrast exists
why_off_catalogue: Blind faults with no surface expression and no strong magnetic throw still load and creep; GPS/Insar strain localization detects the active structure itself. Catalogue maps are built from surface expression, so strain-localized blind faults are systematically under-mapped
differs: geod_* bands appear in the family's feature lists but no site built a strain-primary detector; h20 used tilt-wingcrack mechanics, h16 used topo+geophysics blends dominated by potential-field edges
rank_note: Rank 2: expected +0.005–0.015 if active-fault fraction of hidden set is high; LOW cost (bands already cached). Named mimic: magmatic inflation sources, groundwater withdrawal subsidence

name: H-C Conductivity-cap breach / basement-offset corridor
signature: Lateral conductivity contrasts (clay-cap edges) and basement-thickness offset lines: geothermal upflow alters wall rock to conductive clay; faults juxtapose resistive basement against conductive fill
why_off_catalogue: MT/resistivity imaging sees through cover; basin-bounding faults buried under young sediments show as basement-offset edges with no mapped trace at the surface
differs: h32c used MT clay-cap only as a placement layer on already-decoded dots; no site used cond_surf/depth_to_base gradients as a primary line detector with its own NMS
rank_note: Rank 3: expected +0.005–0.01; LOW cost. Named mimic: saline aquifers, paleolake clay beds

name: H-D Seismicity–lineament intersection node priority
layers: deq_n100a15, ieq_n100a15 × magnetic/gravity edge fields (from H-A/H-B detectors)
signature: Nodes where earthquake-density ridges intersect geophysical lineaments: fault intersections and step-overs focus both strain and permeability, and thus both microseismicity and geothermal upflow
why_off_catalogue: Small-earthquake lineaments reveal buried fault strands that never break the surface; intersection nodes are where unmapped splays branch off mapped faults
differs: As a node-priority rule on top of a decoded surface (not a standalone raster); h34 scatter and h33d analog-stepover placed dots by geometry/analog priors, not by seismicity-intersection evidence
rank_note: Rank 4: emission-priority increment, expected +0.003–0.008 at matched mass; LOW cost. Named mimic: injection-induced seismicity, quarry blasts

name: H-E Scale-persistent ridge extraction (Steger/Frangi) on the GeoDAWN stack
layers: rtp, tmi_hg, tmi_vg, tc, iso_grav_anom_hg/slope at σ = 1–4 px
signature: Line elements whose ridge response persists across scales (narrow dikes, damage-zone edges), rejecting single-scale noise blobs
why_off_catalogue: Narrow faults and dike-fed permeability corridors average out at 100 m but leave multi-scale ridge evidence; persistence separates them from smooth lithologic contacts
differs: xscale-worm-persistence (0.0581) ran a crude version; 66GEMSDOE's LIDAR-01 hypothesis names Steger/Frangi on LiDAR — this variant on the 100 m geophysical stack risks lane overlap and is ranked last until H-A/H-B are banked
rank_note: Rank 5: expected +0.005–0.02 but MEDIUM-HIGH cost and duplication risk with 66 lane; hold behind a drift check
